captions.detailed: A realistic, matte-black bicycle fork and drop handlebar assembly. It features a rigid front fork with two straight blades, a horizontal crown, and a short head tube stub representing the bicycle frame connection. The drop handlebars curve forward and down on both sides, terminating with upright brake levers and hoods. The steering assembly is fully articulated, allowing the handlebars, stem, and fork to rotate smoothly as a single unit around the steerer tube axis.
captions.instruction: Generate a CadQuery model of a realistic bicycle fork and drop handlebar assembly. The model should include a rigid dual-blade fork, a frame stub for mounting, a forward-reaching stem, and curved drop handlebars equipped with brake lever hoods, colored in a sleek matte black.
captions.factory: The code constructs an articulated assembly consisting of three main parts: a fixed frame stub (head tube), a steerable fork, and the handlebar assembly. The frame stub is built from cylindrical and box primitives. The fork is modeled with a central steerer tube, a horizontal crown block, and two vertical, tapered tubular blades. The handlebar assembly is constructed by sweeping a circular profile along a curved path to form the drop bars, then adding box and cylinder primitives for the stem clamp, brake hoods, and levers. A continuous joint connects the frame stub to the steerable fork and handlebar subassembly to allow steering rotation.
